     5	/-!
     6	# Lines, bounded line polynomials, and line-point distributions
     7	
     8	This file provides the seed-bearing line descriptions and coefficient-list
     9	polynomials shared by the observable and combining chapters. It also realizes
    10	the line-point distribution directly from the conditionally linear sampler.
    11	Over a finite coefficient field, bounded individual-degree multivariate
    12	polynomials form a finite outcome set for the associated measurements.
    13	
    14	## References
    15	
    16	The line and bounded-polynomial definitions are blueprint
    17	`def:ideg-deg-polynomials`, with source origin
    18	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:51-58`. The
    19	line-point sampler is `def:line-point-dist` in blueprint chapter 13, from
    20	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:274-287`.
    21	-/
    22	
    23	open scoped BigOperators
    24	
    25	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    26	
    27	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    28	open MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries
    29	
    30	noncomputable section
    31	
    32	/-- A formalization-only identity used to construct canonical line
    33	descriptions: applying the canonical line-representative projection twice has
    34	the same effect as applying it once. -/
    35	theorem lineRepMap_apply_self {K : Type*} [Field K] {m : ℕ}
    36	    (v u : Fin m → K) :
    37	    lineRepMap v (lineRepMap v u) = lineRepMap v u := by
    38	  simp [lineRepMap, canonicalProjOfKernel, LinearMap.comp_apply]
    39	
    40	/-- The two presentations of lines used by the low-degree question sampler. -/
    41	inductive LineKind where
    42	  | axis
    43	  | diagonal
    44	  deriving DecidableEq, Fintype
    45	
    46	/-- A seed-bearing line description for blueprint
    47	`def:line-point-dist`, paper
    48	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:143-174,243-287`.
    49	
    50	An axis description stores its canonical base and seed. A diagonal description
    51	stores only the projected direction, together with its prefix-zero invariant.
    52	Both cases carry the assertion that their base is fixed by the
    53	appropriate `lineRepMap`. Coordinates are numbered from zero; coordinate `j`
    54	corresponds to the paper's coordinate `j + 1`. -/
    55	inductive LineDesc (L : LdParams) where
    56	  | axis (base : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) (seed : ScalarQ L)
    57	      (baseFixed : lineRepMap (coordinateDirection (chiIndex L seed)) base = base)
    58	  | diagonal (base : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) (seed : ScalarQ L)
    59	      (direction : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L)
    60	      (baseFixed : lineRepMap direction base = base)
    61	      (prefixZero : ∀ j : Fin L.m, j.val < (chiIndex L seed).val → direction j = 0)
    62	  deriving DecidableEq
    63	
    64	/-- The tag of a canonical line description. -/
    65	def LineDesc.kind {L : LdParams} : LineDesc L → LineKind
    66	  | .axis _ _ _ => .axis
    67	  | .diagonal _ _ _ _ _ => .diagonal
    68	
    69	/-- The seed retained by a canonical line description. -/
    70	def LineDesc.seed {L : LdParams} : LineDesc L → ScalarQ L
    71	  | .axis _ seed _ => seed
    72	  | .diagonal _ seed _ _ _ => seed
    73	
    74	/-- The canonical base stored by a line description. -/
    75	def LineDesc.base {L : LdParams} : LineDesc L → Fin L.m → ScalarQ L
    76	  | .axis base _ _ => base
    77	  | .diagonal base _ _ _ _ => base
    78	
    79	/-- The geometric direction represented by a canonical line description.
    80	Diagonal descriptions already store the projected data, so this map does
    81	not apply a second projection. -/
    82	def LineDesc.direction {L : LdParams} (line : LineDesc L) :
    83	    Fin L.m → ScalarQ L :=
    84	  match line with
    85	  | .axis _ seed _ => coordinateDirection (chiIndex L seed)
    86	  | .diagonal _ _ direction _ _ => direction
    87	
    88	/-- The canonical base is fixed by the representative map of the line's
    89	geometric direction. -/
    90	theorem LineDesc.base_fixed {L : LdParams} (line : LineDesc L) :
    91	    lineRepMap line.direction line.base = line.base := by
    92	  cases line with
    93	  | axis base seed baseFixed => exact baseFixed
    94	  | diagonal base seed direction baseFixed prefixZero => exact baseFixed
    95	
    96	/-- Every diagonal description carries the source prefix-zero invariant. -/
    97	theorem LineDesc.diagonal_prefix_zero {L : LdParams} (line : LineDesc L)
    98	    (hline : line.kind = .diagonal) :
    99	    ∀ j : Fin L.m, j.val < (chiIndex L line.seed).val → line.direction j = 0 := by
   100	  cases line with
   101	  | axis base seed baseFixed => simp [LineDesc.kind] at hline
   102	  | diagonal base seed direction baseFixed prefixZero => exact prefixZero
   103	
   104	/-- The point set represented by a seed-bearing line description. -/
   105	noncomputable def LineDesc.pointSet {L : LdParams} (line : LineDesc L) :
   106	    Set (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) :=
   107	  linePoints line.base line.direction
   108	
   109	/-- Multivariate polynomials in `m` variables whose total degree is at most
   110	`d`. This is the class `deg_d` in blueprint
   111	`def:ideg-deg-polynomials`, paper
   112	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:51-52`. -/
   113	abbrev TotalDegreePoly (m : ℕ) (K : Type*) [CommSemiring K] (d : ℕ) :=
   114	  {p : MvPolynomial (Fin m) K // p.totalDegree ≤ d}
   115	
   116	/-- Coefficient-list representation of a univariate polynomial of degree at
   117	most `c` over the scalar field of `L`. -/
   118	abbrev DegPoly (L : LdParams) (c : ℕ) := Fin (c + 1) → ScalarQ L
   119	
   120	/-- Extend a coefficient list by zero from degree bound `c` to `c'`. -/
   121	def DegPoly.padTo {L : LdParams} {c c' : ℕ} (_h : c ≤ c')
   122	    (f : DegPoly L c) : DegPoly L c' :=
   123	  fun i =>
   124	    if hi : i.val < c + 1 then f ⟨i.val, hi⟩ else 0
   125	
   126	/-- A line polynomial evaluates to `a` at `u` when `u` has a line parameter
   127	and every such parameter gives the same value.  The universal clause handles
   128	the zero-direction presentation without choosing a sentinel parameter. -/
   129	def EvaluatesTo {L : LdParams} {c : ℕ} (line : LineDesc L)
   130	    (f : DegPoly L c) (u : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) (a : ScalarQ L) : Prop :=
   131	  (∃ t : ScalarQ L, u = line.base + t • line.direction) ∧
   132	    ∀ t : ScalarQ L, u = line.base + t • line.direction → evalCoefficient f t = a
   133	
   134	/-- Partially evaluate a line polynomial at a point. The value is undefined
   135	when the point does not determine an evaluation. This formalization-only
   136	completion is used in blueprint chapter 14; the displayed family at paper
   137	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:197-206` has no bottom outcome. -/
   138	noncomputable def evalOpt {L : LdParams} {c : ℕ} (line : LineDesc L)
   139	    (u : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) (f : DegPoly L c) : Option (ScalarQ L) := by
   140	  classical
   141	  exact if h : ∃ a : ScalarQ L, EvaluatesTo line f u a then
   142	    some (Classical.choose h)
   143	  else none
   144	
   145	/-- Convert an axis-line CL output to its seed-bearing presentation; paper
   146	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:243-257,276-287`. -/
   147	def aLineDescOf (L : LdParams) (line : LdSpace L) : LineDesc L :=
   148	  let direction := coordinateDirection (chiIndex L line.seed)
   149	  let base := lineRepMap direction line.point
   150	  LineDesc.axis base line.seed (lineRepMap_apply_self direction line.point)
   151	
   152	/-- Convert a diagonal-line CL output to its seed-bearing presentation; paper
   153	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:261-287`. -/
   154	def dLineDescOf (L : LdParams) (line : LdSpace L) : LineDesc L :=
   155	  let direction := prefixProjection (chiIndex L line.seed) line.direction
   156	  let base := lineRepMap direction line.point
   157	  LineDesc.diagonal base line.seed direction
   158	    (lineRepMap_apply_self direction line.point) (by
   159	      intro j hj
   160	      change prefixProjection (chiIndex L line.seed) line.direction j = 0
   161	      rw [prefixProjection, if_pos hj])
   162	
   163	/-- The axis-line/point component of the low-degree line-point sampler; paper

    21	/-- On a nonzero direction, completed evaluation agrees with polynomial
    22	evaluation at the unique affine parameter. -/
    23	theorem evalOpt_affine_parameter_of_direction_ne_zero {L : LdParams}
    24	    {bound : ℕ} (line : LineDesc L) (hdir : line.direction ≠ 0)
    25	    (poly : DegPoly L bound) (param : ScalarQ L) :
    26	    evalOpt line (line.base + param • line.direction) poly =
    27	      some (evalCoefficient poly param) := by
    28	  apply WinImplications.evalOpt_eq_some_of_evaluatesTo
    29	  refine ⟨⟨param, rfl⟩, ?_⟩
    30	  intro other heq
    31	  have hsmul : param • line.direction = other • line.direction :=
    32	    add_left_cancel heq
    33	  have hsub : (param - other) • line.direction = 0 := by
    34	    rw [sub_smul, hsmul, sub_self]
    35	  have hparam : param = other :=
    36	    sub_eq_zero.mp ((smul_eq_zero.mp hsub).resolve_right hdir)
    37	  rw [hparam]
    38	
    39	end

     4	/-!
     5	# Uniform collision bounds on nondegenerate affine lines
     6	
     7	This module combines uniqueness of affine evaluation with the univariate
     8	root-count bound to control collisions under a uniform line parameter.
     9

    11	
    12	The result is the Schwartz--Zippel step in `lem:qld-xz-lines`,
    13	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:950-955`.

    24	field size under a uniform affine parameter. -/

    29	      if evalOpt line (line.base + param • line.direction) first =
    30	        evalOpt line (line.base + param • line.direction) second then 1 else 0) ≤
    31	      (bound : ℝ) / Fintype.card (ScalarQ L) := by
    32	  classical
    33	  simp_rw [evalOpt_affine_parameter_of_direction_ne_zero line hdir,

    38	    mul_ite, mul_one, mul_zero, ← Finset.sum_filter]

    40	  exact div_le_div_of_nonneg_right (by exact_mod_cast hcard) (by positivity)

    30	    (hweight : ∀ line, 0 ≤ weight line) (first second : DegPoly L bound)
    31	    (hne : first ≠ second) :
    32	    avgOver (linePointDist L) (fun sample =>
    33	      if sample.1.direction ≠ 0 then weight sample.1 *
    34	        (if evalOpt sample.1 sample.2 first = evalOpt sample.1 sample.2 second

    36	      (bound : ℝ) / Fintype.card (ScalarQ L) *

    48	      (evalOpt_uniform_parameter_collision_le sample.1 hdir first second hne)
    49	      (hweight sample.1)).trans_eq

    28	condition is imposed on the second direction. -/

    33	    (first second : DegPoly L bound) (hne : first ≠ second) :

     3	/-!
     4	# Conditional collision bounds from fiber averages
     5	
     6	This module converts an unnormalized collision estimate on every first-question
     7	fiber into the positive-mass conditional collision predicate used by the
     8	pasting theorem.
     9	
    10	## References
    11	
    12	The conditional collision hypothesis is from `lem:pasting`,
    13	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:504-525`. Its use in
    14	the QPBT combining argument occurs at
    15	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:950-963`.
    16	-/

    18	open scoped BigOperators
    19	
    20	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    21	
    22	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    23	
    24	noncomputable section
    25	
    26	/-- An unnormalized collision estimate on every first-question fiber implies
    27	the positive-mass conditional collision predicate of `lem:pasting`. This is a
    28	formalization-only normalization adapter for paper lines 504--525. -/
    29	theorem collision_bound_of_fiber_averages {X Y₁ Y₂ R₂ Γ₂ : Type*}
    30	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype Y₁] [DecidableEq Y₁]
    31	    [Fintype Y₂] [DecidableEq Y₂] [Fintype R₂] [DecidableEq R₂]
    32	    [Fintype Γ₂] (dist : Distribution ((X × Y₁) × Y₂))
    33	    (eval₂ : Γ₂ → Y₂ → R₂) (eta : ℝ)
    34	    (hbound : ∀ fixed : X × Y₁, ∀ first second : Γ₂, first ≠ second →
    35	      avgOver dist (fun sample => if sample.1 = fixed then
    36	        (if eval₂ first sample.2 = eval₂ second sample.2 then 1 else 0) else 0) ≤
    37	      eta * avgOver dist (fun sample => if sample.1 = fixed then 1 else 0)) :
    38	    HasConditionalCollisionBound dist eval₂ eta := by
    39	  classical
    40	  intro question point _ first second hne
    41	  have havg (value : ((X × Y₁) × Y₂) → ℝ) :
    42	      avgOver dist value = ∑ sample, dist.weight sample * value sample := by
    43	    exact (dist.sum_univ_eq_sum_support _ (fun sample hout => by
    44	      rw [dist.outsideSupport sample hout, zero_mul])).symm
    45	  have hmass : (dist.map Prod.fst).weight (question, point) =
    46	      avgOver dist (fun sample => if sample.1 = (question, point) then 1 else 0) := by
    47	    rw [Distribution.map_weight]
    48	    unfold avgOver
    49	    rw [Finset.sum_filter]
    50	    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    51	    intro sample _
    52	    by_cases hfixed : sample.1 = (question, point) <;> simp [hfixed]
    53	  rw [hmass]
    54	  have h := hbound (question, point) first second hne
    55	  simpa [havg, Fintype.sum_prod_type, mul_ite] using h
    56	
    57	end
    58	
    59	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

   120	\section{The domain of the conditional Lean helper}
   121	
   122	The source statement does not take an arbitrary joint point measurement as an
   123	input.  It uses the family $\{\hat Q^{x,z}_{a,b}\}$ constructed by the preceding
   124	point lemma, whose error has the form $\delta_Q(\eps)=\poly(\eps)$.  Consequently,
   125	an internal theorem which accepts an already constructed point witness must retain
   126	the same quantitative dependency: it should first fix a function
   127	$\delta_Q:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ satisfying the one-variable polynomial-error
   128	predicate, then choose $\delta_P$, and at strategy error $\eps$ accept only a
   129	point witness with bound $\delta_Q(\eps)$.
   130	
   131	Before the repair tracked by \ghissue{389}, the Lean helper
   132	\path{exists_combinedLinesWitness_ofPointsWitness} instead had the quantifier
   133	order
   134	\[
   135	  \exists\delta_P=\poly(\eps,md/q)\quad
   136	  \forall\eps\ \forall\delta_Q\ \forall Q,
   137	  \qquad Q\text{ has point error at most }\delta_Q
   138	  \Longrightarrow T\text{ has line error at most }\delta_P(\eps,md/q).
   139	\]
   140	Thus the line-error function was chosen before an unrestricted scalar
   141	$\delta_Q$, and did not depend on it.  The fields of
   142	\path{CombinedPointsWitness} bound self-consistency and the two ordered-product
   143	comparisons by precisely this scalar; they impose no relation between an
   144	arbitrary $\delta_Q$ and $\eps$.  The conditioned-pasting estimate therefore
   145	cannot eliminate $\delta_Q$ from its conclusion.
   146	
   147	There is a concrete mathematical obstruction to the old domain.  Set
   148	$\eps=0$, take $m=1$ and fixed $d$, and let $q$ grow through admissible field
   149	sizes with $q>d+1$.  On any perfect strategy, define the supplied projective
   150	joint point measurement deterministically, with X answer $x^{d+1}$ and a fixed
   151	Z answer, identically on the two player sides.  Its self-consistency defect is
   152	zero, while the two ordered-product defects are finite and hence can be covered
   153	by a sufficiently large scalar $\delta_Q$, which the old helper quantified
   154	arbitrarily.  On an axis X line, however, every outcome allowed by
   155	\path{CombinedLinesWitness.axis_degree_X} evaluates as a polynomial of degree at
   156	most $d$.  Its difference from $x^{d+1}$ has at most $d+1$ roots, so even after
   157	mixing line outcomes the disagreement probability on that line is at least
   158	$1-(d+1)/q$.  Since axis lines have fixed positive weight in the line-point
   159	law, the resulting line consistency defect stays bounded away from zero as
   160	$q\to\infty$.  In contrast, the two-variable polynomial-error predicate forces
   161	$\delta_P(0,d/q)\to0$.  This argument diagnoses the theorem interface; no Lean
   162	counterexample theorem is asserted here.
   163	
   164	The repaired conditional helper has the form
   165	\[
   166	  \forall\delta_Q,\quad \delta_Q=\poly(\eps)\Longrightarrow
   167	  \exists\delta_P=\poly(\eps,md/q)\quad
   168	  \forall\eps\ \forall Q\text{ with error }\delta_Q(\eps),\quad
   169	  \exists T\text{ with error }\delta_P(\eps,md/q).
   170	\]
   171	This is not a new hypothesis on the paper theorem.  The source-facing Lean
   172	declaration \path{exists_combinedLinesWitness} preserves its original statement:
   173	it existentially obtains $\delta_Q$ and its point witnesses from the preceding
   174	point construction, then applies the conditional helper.
   175	
   176	The remaining construction target is
   177	\path{combined_line_measurement_consistency}. For a joint point family
   178	with error $\delta_Q(\eps)=\poly(\eps)$, it asks for evaluated consistency
   179	of the explicit unconditioned measurement
   180	\[
   181	 T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}_{f_X,f_Z}
   182	 =L^X_{f_X}(\ell_X)L^Z_{f_Z}(\ell_Z)L^X_{f_X}(\ell_X)
   183	\]
   184	under the original product of line-point distributions, with error
   185	$\delta_P(\eps,md/q)=\poly(\eps,md/q)$ and every directed opposite
   186	placement. The point-to-line comparisons at source lines 900--941 and the
   187	pasting argument at lines 942--961 are the intended discharge. The POVM,
   188	axis-degree properties, and X marginal of this same measurement are proved.
   189	
   190	A bound for a measurement conditioned on nondegenerate lines would not by
   191	itself discharge this target. It would also require a defined conditioning
   192	event, its probability, an estimate for the discarded contribution, and a
   193	transfer of the defect back to the unconditioned measurement above under the
   194	original product law. No such transfer is asserted here. In particular,
   195	the preserved conditioned construction is not identified with
   196	\path{combinedLineMeasurement}; its saved proof remains historical work.
   197	The current target retains its explicit unfinished proof, without assuming
   198	any conditioning or transfer result in a source theorem.

   200	\subsection{The extended-line supplied-point obstruction}
   201	
   202	The same quantitative omission remains in the auxiliary
   203	\path{exists_extendedLinesWitness_ofPointsWitness}: a single polynomial error
   204	function is chosen before an arbitrary scalar $\delta_Q$ and every point witness
   205	at that error. Passing from paired points to the extended scalar answer does
   206	not remove this obstruction. The first-route estimate
   207	$C m g(\eps,md/q)$ in
   208	\path{exists_extendedLinesWitness_established_ofPointsWitness} has the same
   209	problem: it still tends to zero at $\eps=0$ with fixed $m,d$ and increasing $q$.
   210	These unrestricted auxiliaries are tracked by \ghissue{509} and \ghissue{511},
   211	respectively. The source instead uses the family constructed by its point lemma,
   212	with $\delta_Q=\poly(\eps)$, and defines the scalar answer by
   213	$c=\alpha a+\beta b$. Claim~17-1 explicitly retains the point error.
   214	\footnote{The source passages are \path{lem:qld-4-10}, \path{lem:qld-4-12}, and
   215	\path{claim:17-1} in
   216	\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex},
   217	lines~689--709, 993--1018, and 1140--1173.}
   218	
   219	Take $m=d=1$, $\eps=0$, and let $q=2^{2k+1}>2$ tend to infinity.
   220	These parameters are admissible. The Pauli basis test has a perfect projective strategy by
   221	\path{lem:pauli-completeness}.\footnote{See
   222	\path{references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex},
   223	lines~1229--1421, for the construction; the statement and its projective Pauli
   224	measurements appear at lines~1232--1255.}
   225	Let $\hat\psi$ be its normalized expanded state. On each player's expanded
   226	local space, define the supplied joint point measurement by
   227	\[
   228	 Q^{x,z}_{a,b}=
   229	 \begin{cases}
   230	   \Id,&(a,b)=(x^2,0),\\
   231	   0,&\text{otherwise}.
   232	 \end{cases}
   233	\]
   234	This is a complete projective measurement and is exactly self-consistent in
   235	every opposite placement. The finitely many averaged squared distances from the
   236	two ordered expanded point products are finite real numbers. Taking their
   237	maximum and zero gives a scalar $\delta_Q$ satisfying all the fields of the
   238	point witness. No estimate of this scalar in terms of $\eps$ is required.
   239	
   240	The extended point answer is $\alpha x^2$. In dimension $2m+2=4$, the directly
   241	indexed line-point law assigns weight $1/2$ to axis lines and then chooses one
   242	of the four coordinates uniformly. Its X-axis branch therefore has mass $1/8$.
   243	On that branch, $z,\alpha,\beta$ are fixed along the line, while $x$ is uniform
   244	in the field. The canonical base has X coordinate zero, so the affine line
   245	parameter is exactly $x$. For $\alpha\ne0$, every permitted line answer $p$
   246	has degree at most one, and $p(X)-\alpha X^2$ is a nonzero polynomial of degree
   247	two. It has at most two roots, hence its agreement with the point answer is at
   248	most $2/q$.
   249	
   250	This bound also holds for any line POVM. Indeed, for a fixed line let $w_p$
   251	be the expectation of its effect for $p$ in the expanded state, at the line
   252	player's placement. Positivity and completeness give $w_p\ge0$ and

    78	  [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K] [Fintype L] [DecidableEq L]

    80	/-- Every bipartite outcome correlation on the independently padded state
    81	equals the correlation of the compressed POVMs on the original state.
    82	Neither normalization nor equality of the player spaces is required. -/
    83	theorem vector_qform_ground_compress_measurement
    84	    (k₀ : K) (l₀ : L) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (I × J))
    85	    (A : Quantum.Measurement α (I × K)) (B : Quantum.Measurement β (J × L))
    86	    (a : α) (b : β) :
    87	    vectorQForm (padState k₀ l₀ ψ) (heteroKron (A.effect a) (B.effect b)) =
    88	      vectorQForm ψ (heteroKron
    89	        ((groundCompressMeasurement k₀ A).effect a)
    90	        ((groundCompressMeasurement l₀ B).effect b)) := by
    91	  exact stateQForm_padState k₀ l₀ ψ _ _ _ _ (fun _ _ => rfl) (fun _ _ => rfl)
    92	
    93	/-- The averaged off-diagonal consistency defect is exactly preserved by
    94	ground-coordinate compression on independently padded bipartite states.
    95	This applies to any finite question distribution and any pair of POVM families. -/
    96	theorem consistency_defect_ground_compress_measurement [DecidableEq α]
    97	    (μ : Distribution X) (k₀ : K) (l₀ : L) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (I × J))
    98	    (A : X → Quantum.Measurement α (I × K))
    99	    (B : X → Quantum.Measurement α (J × L)) :
   100	    consistencyDefect μ
   101	        (fun x a => heteroKron ((A x).effect a) 1)
   102	        (fun x a => heteroKron 1 ((B x).effect a)) (padState k₀ l₀ ψ) =
   103	      consistencyDefect μ
   104	        (fun x a => heteroKron ((groundCompressMeasurement k₀ (A x)).effect a) 1)
   105	        (fun x a => heteroKron 1 ((groundCompressMeasurement l₀ (B x)).effect a)) ψ := by
   106	  unfold consistencyDefect
   107	  apply avgOver_congr
   108	  intro x
   109	  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   110	  intro a _
   111	  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   112	  intro b _
   113	  split_ifs with hab
   114	  · rfl
   115	  · simp only [heteroKron_mul, mul_one, one_mul]
   116	    exact vector_qform_ground_compress_measurement k₀ l₀ ψ (A x) (B x) a b
   117	
   118	/-- A consistency bound holds on the independently padded state if and only
   119	if the same bound holds for the compressed measurements on the original state. -/
   120	theorem is_consistent_within_ground_compress_measurement_iff [DecidableEq α]
   121	    (μ : Distribution X) (k₀ : K) (l₀ : L) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (I × J))
   122	    (A : X → Quantum.Measurement α (I × K))
   123	    (B : X → Quantum.Measurement α (J × L)) (δ : ℝ) :
   124	    IsConsistentWithin μ
   125	        (fun x a => heteroKron ((A x).effect a) 1)
   126	        (fun x a => heteroKron 1 ((B x).effect a)) (padState k₀ l₀ ψ) δ ↔
   127	      IsConsistentWithin μ
   128	        (fun x a => heteroKron ((groundCompressMeasurement k₀ (A x)).effect a) 1)
   129	        (fun x a => heteroKron 1 ((groundCompressMeasurement l₀ (B x)).effect a)) ψ δ := by
   130	  unfold IsConsistentWithin
   131	  rw [consistency_defect_ground_compress_measurement]
   132	
   133	/-- Exact consistency preservation also holds after question-dependent
   134	postprocessing. The original outcome types and the two outcome maps may
   135	differ; only the final outcome alphabet is shared. In the application to
   136	`lem:qld-4-7`, these maps include evaluation of the polynomial outcomes. -/
   137	theorem consistency_defect_ground_compress_measurement_postprocess
   138	    {γ : Type*} [Fintype γ] [DecidableEq γ] [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
   139	    (μ : Distribution X) (k₀ : K) (l₀ : L) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (I × J))
   140	    (A : X → Quantum.Measurement α (I × K))
   141	    (B : X → Quantum.Measurement β (J × L)) (f : X → α → γ) (g : X → β → γ) :
   142	    consistencyDefect μ
   143	        (fun x c => heteroKron (((A x).postprocess (f x)).effect c) 1)
   144	        (fun x c => heteroKron 1 (((B x).postprocess (g x)).effect c))
   145	        (padState k₀ l₀ ψ) =
   146	      consistencyDefect μ
   147	        (fun x c => heteroKron
   148	          (((groundCompressMeasurement k₀ (A x)).postprocess (f x)).effect c) 1)
   149	        (fun x c => heteroKron 1
   150	          (((groundCompressMeasurement l₀ (B x)).postprocess (g x)).effect c)) ψ := by
   151	  simpa only [ground_compress_measurement_postprocess] using
   152	    consistency_defect_ground_compress_measurement μ k₀ l₀ ψ
   153	      (fun x => (A x).postprocess (f x)) (fun x => (B x).postprocess (g x))
   154	
   155	end Bipartite

   157	/-- Compressing the existing completed Naimark dilation at `none` recovers
   158	the original POVM as a measurement, by its established effect identity. -/
   159	@[simp] theorem ground_compress_dilated_measurement
   160	    {α I : Type} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I]
   161	    (a₀ : α) (M : Quantum.Measurement α I) :
   162	    groundCompressMeasurement none (dilatedMeasurement a₀ M) = M := by
   163	  apply Quantum.Measurement.ext
   164	  intro a
   165	  ext i j
   166	  exact dilatedMeasurement_compression a₀ a M i j
   167	
   168	end

     3	/-!
     4	# Ground-slice compression of measurements
     5	
     6	This module restricts a POVM on a product space to one distinguished ancillary
     7	coordinate. It also records that this restriction commutes with deterministic
     8	outcome postprocessing, recovers a POVM from its one-measurement Naimark
     9	dilation, and preserves consistency defects evaluated on the correspondingly
    10	padded bipartite state.
    11	
    12	The construction supports the pullback after the first paragraph of the proof
    13	of paper `lem:qld-4-7`,
    14	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1279-1289`.
    15	-/
    16	
    17	open scoped BigOperators Matrix MatrixOrder ComplexOrder
    18	
    19	namespace MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement
    20	
    21	/-- Restrict every effect of a POVM to the matrix block at one fixed ancillary
    22	coordinate. The principal submatrix of a positive semidefinite effect remains
    23	positive semidefinite, and restricting the sum of the effects restricts the
    24	identity to the identity. -/
    25	noncomputable def compressAt
    26	    {Outcome I κ : Type*}
    27	    [Fintype Outcome] [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I]
    28	    [Fintype κ] [DecidableEq κ]
    29	    (k₀ : κ) (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement Outcome (I × κ)) :
    30	    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement Outcome I :=
    31	  MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.ofSumEqOne
    32	    (fun a => (M.effect a).submatrix (fun i => (i, k₀)) (fun i => (i, k₀)))
    33	    (fun a => Matrix.nonneg_iff_posSemidef.mpr
    34	      ((Matrix.nonneg_iff_posSemidef.mp (M.pos a)).submatrix (fun i => (i, k₀))))
    35	    (by
    36	      classical
    37	      ext i j
    38	      simpa only [Matrix.sum_apply, Matrix.submatrix_apply, Matrix.one_apply,
    39	        Prod.mk.injEq, and_true]
    40	        using congrFun (congrFun M.sum_eq_one (i, k₀)) (j, k₀))
    41	
    42	@[simp] theorem compressAt_effect
    43	    {Outcome I κ : Type*}
    44	    [Fintype Outcome] [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I]
    45	    [Fintype κ] [DecidableEq κ]
    46	    (k₀ : κ) (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement Outcome (I × κ)) (a : Outcome) :
    47	    (M.compressAt k₀).effect a =
    48	      (M.effect a).submatrix (fun i => (i, k₀)) (fun i => (i, k₀)) :=
    49	  rfl
    50	
    51	/-- Restricting a POVM to a fixed ancillary coordinate commutes with
    52	deterministic relabeling of its outcomes. -/
    53	theorem compressAt_postprocess
    54	    {A B I κ : Type*}
    55	    [Fintype A] [DecidableEq A] [Fintype B] [DecidableEq B]
    56	    [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I] [Fintype κ] [DecidableEq κ]
    57	    (k₀ : κ) (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement A (I × κ)) (f : A → B) :
    58	    (M.postprocess f).compressAt k₀ = (M.compressAt k₀).postprocess f := by
    59	  classical
    60	  apply MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.ext
    61	  intro b
    62	  ext i j
    63	  simp only [compressAt_effect, MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.postprocess_effect,
    64	    Matrix.submatrix_apply, Matrix.sum_apply]
    65	
    66	end MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement
    67	
    68	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    69	
    70	open MIPStarRE.LDT MIPStarRE.Quantum
    71	
    72	namespace Measurement
    73	
    74	/-- Compressing the completed one-measurement Naimark dilation at its
    75	distinguished `none` coordinate recovers the original POVM. -/
    76	theorem compressAt_dilatedMeasurement
    77	    {A I : Type} [Fintype A] [DecidableEq A]
    78	    [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I]
    79	    (a₀ : A) (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement A I) :
    80	    (dilatedMeasurement a₀ M).compressAt none = M := by
    81	  apply MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.ext
    82	  intro a
    83	  ext i j
    84	  exact dilatedMeasurement_compression a₀ a M i j
    85	
    86	end Measurement
    87	
    88	/-- Ground-slice compression preserves exactly the off-diagonal consistency
    89	defect when the bipartite state is padded at the same two ancillary
    90	coordinates. This is an equality of POVM correlations and does not assert that
    91	the compressed measurements are projective. -/
    92	theorem consistencyDefect_padState_compressAt
    93	    {X Outcome I J κA κB : Type*}
    94	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X]
    95	    [Fintype Outcome] [DecidableEq Outcome]
    96	    [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I] [Fintype J] [DecidableEq J]
    97	    [Fintype κA] [DecidableEq κA] [Fintype κB] [DecidableEq κB]
    98	    (μ : Distribution X)
    99	    (MA : X → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement Outcome (I × κA))
   100	    (MB : X → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement Outcome (J × κB))
   101	    (a₀ : κA) (b₀ : κB) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (I × J)) :
   102	    consistencyDefect μ
   103	        (fun x a => heteroKron ((MA x).effect a) 1)
   104	        (fun x a => heteroKron 1 ((MB x).effect a))
   105	        (padState a₀ b₀ ψ) =
   106	      consistencyDefect μ
   107	        (fun x a => heteroKron (((MA x).compressAt a₀).effect a) 1)
   108	        (fun x a => heteroKron 1 (((MB x).compressAt b₀).effect a))
   109	        ψ := by
   110	  unfold consistencyDefect
   111	  apply avgOver_congr
   112	  intro x
   113	  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   114	  intro a _
   115	  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   116	  intro b _
   117	  by_cases hab : a = b
   118	  · simp [hab]
   119	  · simp only [hab, if_false]
   120	    change vectorQForm (padState a₀ b₀ ψ)
   121	        (heteroKron ((MA x).effect a) 1 * heteroKron 1 ((MB x).effect b)) =
   122	      vectorQForm ψ
   123	        (heteroKron (((MA x).compressAt a₀).effect a) 1 *
   124	          heteroKron 1 (((MB x).compressAt b₀).effect b))
   125	    simpa only [heteroKron_mul, Matrix.mul_one, Matrix.one_mul] using
   126	      stateQForm_padState a₀ b₀ ψ
   127	        (((MA x).compressAt a₀).effect a)
   128	        (((MB x).compressAt b₀).effect b)
   129	        ((MA x).effect a) ((MB x).effect b)
   130	        (fun i j => rfl) (fun i j => rfl)
   131	
   132	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

     3	/-!
     4	# Completion on a prescribed set of outcomes
     5	
     6	This formalization-only auxiliary constructs a complete measurement supported on
     7	the good outcomes of a finite measurement, by sending every bad outcome to a
     8	specified good outcome. For projective measurements this adds the complementary
     9	projection to the default effect and preserves projectivity. The consistency
    10	estimates charge changes of outcome labels only to the state mass of that
    11	complementary projection, on either of two possibly different player spaces.
    12	
    13	The source-specific estimate on the mass outside the image of the polynomial
    14	combining map is the unimplemented target `global_polynomial_bad_mass_le`,
    15	specified in `audits/2026-09-06_supported-projective-completion.md` under issue #279.
    16	No result here asserts the global polynomial-pair theorem or derives that estimate.
    17	
    18	## References
    19	
    20	* `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1364-1402`,
    21	  the completion step after `eq:qld-sgg-mhat-sandwich` in `lem:qld-4-7`.
    22	* Blueprint `lem:qld-4-7`, whose source theorem remains separate from this auxiliary.
    23	-/
    24	
    25	open scoped BigOperators MatrixOrder Matrix ComplexOrder
    26	
    27	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT.SupportedCompletion
    28	
    29	open MIPStarRE.LDT hiding Measurement
    30	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
    31	open DistanceCalculus
    32	
    33	variable {α β X ι ιA ιB : Type*}
    34	variable [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β]
    35	variable [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X]
    36	variable [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    37	variable [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
    38	
    39	/-- Retain every good outcome and send every other outcome to the specified
    40	good outcome. The default is actual domain data, with its membership proof. -/
    41	def toGood (good : α → Prop) [DecidablePred good]
    42	    (a₀ : {a // good a}) (a : α) : {a // good a} :=
    43	  if h : good a then ⟨a, h⟩ else a₀
    44	
    45	omit [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] in
    46	@[simp] theorem toGood_coe (good : α → Prop) [DecidablePred good]
    47	    (a₀ a : {a // good a}) : toGood good a₀ a = a := by
    48	  simp [toGood, a.property]
    49	
    50	/-- The omitted effects. When the measurement is projective, their sum is the
    51	projection complementary to the sum of good effects. -/
    52	noncomputable def badEffect (M : Measurement α ι)
    53	    (good : α → Prop) [DecidablePred good] : Op ι :=
    54	  ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => ¬ good a), M.effect a
    55	
    56	/-- Complete the restriction to good outcomes by adding all bad effects to
    57	`a₀`. This is an outcome postprocessing of the original complete measurement. -/
    58	noncomputable def complete (M : Measurement α ι)
    59	    (good : α → Prop) [DecidablePred good] (a₀ : {a // good a}) :
    60	    Measurement {a // good a} ι :=
    61	  M.postprocess (toGood good a₀)
    62	
    63	/-- The completion is projective whenever the original measurement is
    64	projective, by projectivity of outcome postprocessing. -/
    65	theorem complete_isProjective (M : Measurement α ι)
    66	    (hM : Measurement.IsProjective M) (good : α → Prop) [DecidablePred good]
    67	    (a₀ : {a // good a}) : Measurement.IsProjective (complete M good a₀) :=
    68	  SandwichProduct.postprocess_isProjective M hM (toGood good a₀)
    69	
    70	omit [DecidableEq α] in
    71	/-- The bad effect is precisely the complement of the restricted total. -/
    72	theorem badEffect_eq_one_sub (M : Measurement α ι)
    73	    (good : α → Prop) [DecidablePred good] :
    74	    badEffect M good = 1 - ∑ a : {a // good a}, M.effect a := by
    75	  have hsplit := Fintype.sum_subtype_add_sum_subtype good M.effect
    76	  have hbad : badEffect M good = ∑ a : {a // ¬ good a}, M.effect a := by
    77	    exact Finset.sum_subtype _ (by simp) M.effect
    78	  rw [hbad]
    79	  rw [M.sum_eq_one] at hsplit
    80	  exact eq_sub_of_add_eq' hsplit
    81	
    82	omit [DecidableEq α] in
    83	/-- The sum of the omitted effects is positive semidefinite. -/
    84	theorem badEffect_nonneg (M : Measurement α ι)
    85	    (good : α → Prop) [DecidablePred good] : 0 ≤ badEffect M good :=
    86	  Finset.sum_nonneg fun a _ => M.pos a
    87	
    88	/-- The submeasurement obtained by retaining only the good outcomes. -/
    89	noncomputable def restrict (M : Measurement α ι)
    90	    (good : α → Prop) [DecidablePred good] : Submeasurement {a // good a} ι where
    91	  effect a := M.effect a
    92	  pos a := M.pos a
    93	  sum_le_one := by
    94	    have h := badEffect_nonneg M good
    95	    rw [badEffect_eq_one_sub] at h
    96	    exact sub_nonneg.mp h
    97	
    98	/-- The bad effect is itself a projection: it is one effect of the binary
    99	postprocessing recording whether an outcome is bad. -/
   100	theorem badEffect_isStarProjection (M : Measurement α ι)
   101	    (hM : Measurement.IsProjective M) (good : α → Prop) [DecidablePred good] :
   102	    IsStarProjection (badEffect M good) := by
   103	  have h := SandwichProduct.postprocess_isProjective M hM
   104	    (fun a => decide (¬ good a)) true
   105	  change IsStarProjection (∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter
   106	    (fun a => decide (¬ good a) = true), M.effect a) at h
   107	  simpa only [decide_eq_true_eq, badEffect] using h
   108	
   109	/-- The completed default effect absorbs exactly the omitted projection;
   110	all other good effects are retained. -/
   111	theorem complete_effect (M : Measurement α ι)
   112	    (good : α → Prop) [DecidablePred good] (a₀ a : {a // good a}) :
   113	    (complete M good a₀).effect a =
   114	      M.effect a + if a = a₀ then badEffect M good else 0 := by
   115	  classical
   116	  rw [complete, Measurement.postprocess_effect, Finset.sum_filter]
   117	  have hterm (b : α) :
   118	      (if toGood good a₀ b = a then M.effect b else 0) =
   119	        (if b = a.val then M.effect b else 0) +
   120	          if a = a₀ then (if ¬ good b then M.effect b else 0) else 0 := by
   121	    by_cases hb : good b
   122	    · have heq : toGood good a₀ b = a ↔ b = a.val := by
   123	        simp [toGood, hb, Subtype.ext_iff]
   124	      simp [heq, hb]
   125	    · have hba : b ≠ a.val := by
   126	        rintro rfl
   127	        exact hb a.property
   128	      simp [toGood, hb, hba, eq_comm]
   129	  simp_rw [hterm]
   130	  rw [Finset.sum_add_distrib]
   131	  simp [badEffect, Finset.sum_filter, Finset.sum_ite_irrel]
   132	
   133	/-- Relabeling the completed measurement adds the bad effect to exactly the
   134	label of the chosen default outcome, relative to the relabeled restriction. -/
   135	theorem complete_postprocess_effect (M : Measurement α ι)
   136	    (good : α → Prop) [DecidablePred good] (a₀ : {a // good a})
   137	    (g : {a // good a} → β) (b : β) :
   138	    ((complete M good a₀).postprocess g).effect b =
   139	      ((restrict M good).postprocess g).effect b +
   140	        if b = g a₀ then badEffect M good else 0 := by
   141	  rw [MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.postprocess_effect]
   142	  simp_rw [complete_effect]
   143	  rw [Finset.sum_add_distrib]
   144	  congr 1
   145	  simp [eq_comm]

   147	private theorem postprocess_overlap (M : Measurement α ι) (N : Measurement β ι)
   148	    (f : α → β) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
   149	    (∑ b, stateQForm ψ ((M.postprocess f).effect b * N.effect b)) =
   150	      ∑ a, stateQForm ψ (M.effect a * N.effect (f a)) := by
   151	  simp only [MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.postprocess_effect, Finset.sum_mul,
   152	    stateQForm_finset_sum]
   153	  calc
   154	    (∑ b, ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b),
   155	        stateQForm ψ (M.effect a * N.effect b)) =
   156	      ∑ b, ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b),
   157	        stateQForm ψ (M.effect a * N.effect (f a)) := by
   158	          apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   159	          intro b _
   160	          apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   161	          intro a ha
   162	          rw [(Finset.mem_filter.mp ha).2]
   163	    _ = _ := Finset.sum_fiberwise Finset.univ f _

   165	private theorem postprocess_defect (μ : Distribution X) (M : Measurement α ι)
   166	    (N : X → Measurement β ι) (f : X → α → β) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
   167	    consistencyDefect μ (fun x a => (M.postprocess (f x)).effect a)
   168	        (fun x a => (N x).effect a) ψ =
   169	      avgOver μ (fun x => ‖ψ‖ ^ 2 -
   170	        ∑ a, stateQForm ψ (M.effect a * (N x).effect (f x a))) := by
   171	  unfold consistencyDefect
   172	  simp_rw [consistency_term_eq_stateQForm, point_defect_eq, postprocess_overlap]
   173	
   174	private theorem leftPlaced_postprocess (M : Measurement α ιA) (f : α → β) :
   175	    leftPlacedMeasurement (ιB := ιB) (M.postprocess f) =
   176	      (leftPlacedMeasurement (ιB := ιB) M).postprocess f := by
   177	  apply MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.ext
   178	  intro b
   179	  exact heteroKron_finset_sum_left _ _ _

   181	private theorem rightPlaced_postprocess (M : Measurement α ιB) (f : α → β) :
   182	    rightPlacedMeasurement (ιA := ιA) (M.postprocess f) =
   183	      (rightPlacedMeasurement (ιA := ιA) M).postprocess f := by
   184	  apply MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.ext
   185	  intro b
   186	  exact heteroKron_finset_sum_right _ _ _

   188	private theorem left_postprocess_defect (μ : Distribution X) (M : Measurement α ιA)
   189	    (N : X → Measurement β ιB) (f : X → α → β)
   190	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)) :
   191	    consistencyDefect μ (fun x a => heteroKron ((M.postprocess (f x)).effect a) 1)

   196	    (fun x a => (leftPlacedMeasurement (M.postprocess (f x))).effect a)

     4	/-!
     5	# Projective rounding through outcome postprocessing
     6	
     7	Consistent complete POVMs on two possibly different local spaces have projective
     8	roundings on those same spaces. Their consistency with an opposite-player POVM
     9	survives every question-dependent outcome map, with error
    10	`δ + sqrt (220 * δ^(1/4)) + 2 * sqrt (δ + η)` when the original consistency errors
    11	are at most `δ` and `η`. The estimate is independent of both local dimensions and
    12	the number of outcomes.
    13	
    14	These are formalization-only auxiliary results for the compression and rounding
    15	argument preceding the polynomial-support argument in `lem:qld-4-7`. They do not
    16	construct the global polynomial-pair measurement.

+    {FirstOutcome SecondOutcome FirstLabel SecondLabel FirstSpace SecondSpace : Type*}

+    [Fintype SecondOutcome] [DecidableEq SecondOutcome]
+    [Fintype FirstLabel] [DecidableEq FirstLabel]
+    [Fintype SecondLabel] [DecidableEq SecondLabel]
+    [Fintype FirstSpace] [DecidableEq FirstSpace]

 private theorem tensorMeasurement_isProjective
     {α β I J : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype β]
     [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I] [Fintype J] [DecidableEq J]
     (A : Measurement α I) (B : Measurement β J)
     (hA : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective A)
     (hB : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective B) :
     MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (tensorMeasurement A B) := by
   intro ab
   change IsProj (Matrix.kronecker (A.effect ab.1) (B.effect ab.2))
   refine { isIdempotentElem := ?_, isSelfAdjoint := ?_ }
   · calc
       Matrix.kronecker (A.effect ab.1) (B.effect ab.2) *

   541	\subsection{The class $\MIP^*$}
   542	
   543	The complexity class $\MIP^*$ of \emph{multi-prover interactive proof
   544	  systems with entangled provers} is the class of languages that can be
   545	decided by a \emph{proof system} in which a polynomial-time classical
   546	\emph{verifier} interacts with noncommunicating, computationally unbounded
   547	 \emph{provers} who may share a \emph{finite-dimensional} entangled state. In general there may be polynomially many provers,
   548	and the verifier may interact with them over polynomially many
   549	rounds. In each round, the verifier generates a question for
   550	each prover and receives a response from them. At the end of
   551	the interaction the verifier 
   552	decides to either accept or reject. A language $L$ is in $\MIP^*$ if for
   553	every input $z \in L$, there exists a strategy that the provers can
   554	use to convince the verifier to accept with high probability ($\geq 2/3$), and for every input $z \not\in L$, there is
   555	\emph{no} strategy that the provers can use to convince the verifier
   556	to accept with more than low probability ($\geq 1/3$). The former
   557	property is called \emph{completeness} of the proof system, and the
   558	latter \emph{soundness}. The
   559	completeness and soundness probabilities $2/3$ and $1/3$ may be
   560	amplified by sequentially repeating the protocol. 
   561	
   562	For a formal definition of the class $\MIP^*$, see e.g.~\cite[Section
   563	  6.1]{vidick2016quantum}. 
   564	The main result of this paper is a lower bound, and for this purpose,
   565	it suffices  to restrict our attention to proof
   566	systems which involve only two provers, one round of interaction, and
   567	completeness probability $1$. This class is often denoted $\MIP^*_{1,1/2}(2,1)$. A formal definition for this restricted setting follows. 
   568	
   569	\begin{definition}\label{def:mipstar}
   570	  A language $L$ is in $\MIP^*_{1,1/2}$ if and only if there exist two randomized Turing machines
   571	  $\sampler$ and $\decider$ with the following properties.
   572	  \begin{enumerate}
   573	    \item \textbf{Efficiency:} For every $z\in\{0,1\}^*$ there is
   574	      a game $\game_z = (\cal{X}, \cal{Y}, \cal{A}, \cal{B}, \mu, D)$
   575	      such that:
   576	      \begin{enumerate}
   577	      \item The Turing machine $\sampler$ given input $z$ runs in time $\poly(|z|)$ and returns a
   578	      pair $(x,y) \in \cal{X} \times \cal{Y}$ such that the distribution of $(x,y)$, over the random choices of $\sampler$, is $\mu$.
   579	    \item The Turing machine $\decider$ given as input $z$ and a tuple $(x,y,a,b)
   580	      \in \cal{X} \times \cal{Y} \times \cal{A} \times \cal{B}$ runs in time $\poly(|z|)$ and returns $D(x,y,a,b)$.\footnote{Note that the running time of $\decider$ should be $\poly(|z|)$, even for long inputs $a,b$. This can be ensured by having $D$ return $0$ whenever $x,y,a,b$ are too long with respect to $|z|$.}
   581	    \end{enumerate}
   582	  \item \textbf{Completeness:} If $z \in L$, then $\val^*(\game_z) = 1$
   583	  \item \textbf{Soundness:} If $z \not\in L$, then $\val^*(\game_z) \leq 1/2$.
   584	  \end{enumerate}
   585	  We say that the pair $(\sampler, \decider)$ form an $\MIP^*$
   586	  \emph{verifier} for the language $L$, and the associated family of
   587	  games $\game_z$ are an $\MIP^*$ protocol for $L$.
   588	\end{definition}
   589	
   590	  It is clear that $\MIP^*_{1,1/2}(2,1) \subseteq \MIP^*$ (the
   591	  probability $1/2$ of acceptance of inputs not in the language may be
   592	  reduced to $1/3$ by sequential repetition as noted above). The main result of this paper is that $\RE
   593	  \subseteq \MIP^*_{1,1/2}(2,1)$. Since it is known that $\MIP*\subseteq \RE$ it follows
   594	  that $\MIP^*_{1,1/2}(2,1) = \MIP^* = \RE$. 
   595	
   596	 To show our lower bound it will suffice to consider an even more restricted class of $\MIP^*$
   597	  verifiers, for which the Turing machines $\sampler$ and
   598	  $\decider$ have a special structure which we refer to as

+import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Games.DistanceTheorems.ProjectiveRounding
+import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Games.DistanceTheorems.Calculus
+
+/-!
+# Projective rounding through outcome postprocessing
+
+Consistent complete POVMs on two possibly different local spaces have projective
+roundings on those same spaces. Their consistency with an opposite-player POVM
+survives every question-dependent outcome map, with error
+`δ + sqrt (220 * δ^(1/4)) + 2 * sqrt (δ + η)` when the original consistency errors
+are at most `δ` and `η`. The estimate is independent of both local dimensions and
+the number of outcomes.
+
+These are formalization-only auxiliary results for the compression and rounding
+argument preceding the polynomial-support argument in `lem:qld-4-7`. They do not
+construct the global polynomial-pair measurement.
+
+## References
+
+- `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:135-145`, `lem:ortho`
+- `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1278-1288`,
+  in the proof of `lem:qld-4-7`
+- `references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:389-401`,
+  `fact:triangle-for-simeq` and `fact:data-processing`
+- Issue #278
+- `audits/2026-09-06_rounding_transport.md`
+-/
+
+open scoped BigOperators Matrix MatrixOrder ComplexOrder
+
+namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
+
+open MIPStarRE.LDT hiding Measurement
+open MIPStarRE.Quantum DistanceCalculus
+
+noncomputable section
+
+/-- Formalization-only question-dependent form of `fact:data-processing`.
+Applying the same outcome map to both players at each question cannot increase
+their consistency defect. No normalization of the distribution or state is needed. -/
+theorem consistencyDefect_postprocess_question_le {X α β ιA ιB : Type*}
+    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
+    [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β]
+    [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
+    (μ : Distribution X) (A : X → Measurement α ιA)
+    (B : X → Measurement α ιB) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB))
+    (f : X → α → β) :
+    consistencyDefect μ
+        (fun x b => heteroKron (((A x).postprocess (f x)).effect b) 1)
+        (fun x b => heteroKron 1 (((B x).postprocess (f x)).effect b)) ψ ≤
+      consistencyDefect μ (fun x a => heteroKron ((A x).effect a) 1)
+        (fun x a => heteroKron 1 ((B x).effect a)) ψ := by
+  unfold consistencyDefect
+  apply avgOver_mono
+  intro x
+  simpa only [consistencyDefect,
+    avgOver_const_of_isProbability _ (uniformDistribution_isProbability Unit)] using
+    consistencyDefect_postprocess_le (uniformDistribution Unit)
+      (fun _ => A x) (fun _ => B x) ψ (f x)
+
+private theorem consistencyDefect_const_eq {X α ι : Type*}
+    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
+    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
+    (μ : Distribution X) (hμ : μ.IsProbability)
+    (A B : α → Op ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
+    consistencyDefect μ (fun _ => A) (fun _ => B) ψ =
+      consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution Unit) (fun _ => A) (fun _ => B) ψ := by
+  unfold consistencyDefect
+  rw [avgOver_const_of_isProbability μ hμ,
+    avgOver_const_of_isProbability _ (uniformDistribution_isProbability Unit)]
+
+private theorem consistencyDefect_placed_eq_one_sub_overlap {X α ιA ιB : Type*}
+    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
+    [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
+    (μ : Distribution X) (A : X → Measurement α ιA) (B : X → Measurement α ιB)
+    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)) (hμ : μ.IsProbability) (hψ : ‖ψ‖ = 1) :
+    consistencyDefect μ (fun x a => heteroKron ((A x).effect a) 1)
+        (fun x a => heteroKron 1 ((B x).effect a)) ψ =
+      1 - avgOver μ (fun x => ∑ a, stateQForm ψ
+        (heteroKron ((A x).effect a) ((B x).effect a))) := by
+  simpa only [leftPlacedMeasurement, rightPlacedMeasurement,
+    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.ofSumEqOne, placed_product_stateQForm_eq] using
+    consistencyDefect_eq_one_sub_overlap μ
+      (fun x => leftPlacedMeasurement (A x)) (fun x => rightPlacedMeasurement (B x))
+      ψ hμ hψ
+
+/-- The overlap estimate converts a same-space squared-distance bound into a
+square-root loss in consistency with the unchanged opposite-player POVM. -/
+private theorem rounding_consistency_le {ιA ιB α : Type*}
+    [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
+    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
+    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)) (hψ : ‖ψ‖ = 1)
+    (P A : Measurement α ιA) (B : Measurement α ιB) (δ r : ℝ)
+    (hcons : consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution Unit)
+      (fun _ a => heteroKron (A.effect a) 1)
+      (fun _ a => heteroKron 1 (B.effect a)) ψ ≤ δ)
+    (hdist : opFamilyDistSq (uniformDistribution Unit)
+      (fun _ a => heteroKron (P.effect a) 1)
+      (fun _ a => heteroKron (A.effect a) 1) ψ ≤ r) :
+    consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution Unit)
+      (fun _ a => heteroKron (P.effect a) 1)
+      (fun _ a => heteroKron 1 (B.effect a)) ψ ≤ δ + Real.sqrt r := by
+  letI : Nonempty (ιA × ιB) := by
+    by_contra hι
+    letI : IsEmpty (ιA × ιB) := not_nonempty_iff.mp hι
+    have hzero : ψ = 0 := Subsingleton.elim _ _
+    rw [hzero, norm_zero] at hψ
+    norm_num at hψ
+  have hgap := overlap_gap_le_of_opFamilyDistSq (uniformDistribution Unit)
+    (fun _ => rightPlacedMeasurement B) (fun _ => leftPlacedMeasurement A)
+    (fun _ => leftPlacedMeasurement P) ψ (uniformDistribution_isProbability Unit)
+    hψ r (by
+      simpa only [leftPlacedMeasurement, MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.ofSumEqOne,
+        opFamilyDistSq_symm] using hdist)
+  rw [consistencyDefect_placed_eq_one_sub_overlap (uniformDistribution Unit)
+    (fun _ => A) (fun _ => B)
+    ψ (uniformDistribution_isProbability Unit) hψ] at hcons
+  rw [consistencyDefect_placed_eq_one_sub_overlap (uniformDistribution Unit)
+    (fun _ => P) (fun _ => B)
+    ψ (uniformDistribution_isProbability Unit) hψ]
+  simp only [leftPlacedMeasurement, rightPlacedMeasurement,
+    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.ofSumEqOne] at hgap
+  change |avgOver (uniformDistribution Unit) (fun _ => ∑ a,
+      stateQForm ψ (rightTensor (B.effect a) * leftTensor (A.effect a))) -
+    avgOver (uniformDistribution Unit) (fun _ => ∑ a,
+      stateQForm ψ (rightTensor (B.effect a) * leftTensor (P.effect a)))| ≤ _ at hgap
+  simp only [rightTensor_mul_leftTensor_eq_opTensor] at hgap
+  dsimp only [opTensor, heteroKron] at hgap hcons ⊢
+  have hdiff := (le_abs_self _).trans hgap
+  linarith
+
+/-- Formalization-only transport of the rounding supplied by `lem:ortho`.
+The projective measurement is chosen before the question distribution, outcome
+maps, comparison measurements, and comparison error. The unit-state and
+probability hypotheses give total mass one; only `δ ≥ 0` is required of the
+rounding error, and no upper range bound on either error is used. This supports
+the compression step in `lem:qld-4-7`, not its global-witness conclusion. -/
+theorem projective_rounding_preserves_postprocessed_consistency_left
+    {ιA ιB α : Type*}
+    [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
+    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
+    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)) (hψ : ‖ψ‖ = 1)
+    (A : Measurement α ιA) (B : Measurement α ιB) (δ : ℝ) (hδ : 0 ≤ δ)
+    (hcons : consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution Unit)
+      (fun _ a => heteroKron (A.effect a) 1)
+      (fun _ a => heteroKron 1 (B.effect a)) ψ ≤ δ) :
+    ∃ P : Measurement α ιA, Measurement.IsProjective P ∧
+      opFamilyDistSq (uniformDistribution Unit)
+        (fun _ a => heteroKron (P.effect a) 1)
+        (fun _ a => heteroKron (A.effect a) 1) ψ ≤
+          220 * Real.rpow δ (1 / 4 : ℝ) ∧
+      ∀ {X β : Type*} [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β]
+        (μ : Distribution X), μ.IsProbability → ∀ (f : X → α → β)
+        (N : X → Measurement β ιB) (η : ℝ),
+        consistencyDefect μ
+          (fun x b => heteroKron ((A.postprocess (f x)).effect b) 1)
+          (fun x b => heteroKron 1 ((N x).effect b)) ψ ≤ η →
+        consistencyDefect μ
+          (fun x b => heteroKron ((P.postprocess (f x)).effect b) 1)
+          (fun x b => heteroKron 1 ((N x).effect b)) ψ ≤
+            δ + Real.sqrt (220 * Real.rpow δ (1 / 4 : ℝ)) +
+              2 * Real.sqrt (δ + η) := by
+  obtain ⟨P, hP, hdist⟩ :=
+    projective_rounding_with_explicit_constant ψ hψ A B δ hδ hcons
+  refine ⟨P, hP, hdist, ?_⟩
+  intro X β _ _ _ _ μ hμ f N η hAN
+  have hPB := rounding_consistency_le ψ hψ P A B δ _ hcons hdist
+  have hABf : consistencyDefect μ
+      (fun x b => heteroKron ((A.postprocess (f x)).effect b) 1)
+      (fun x b => heteroKron 1 ((B.postprocess (f x)).effect b)) ψ ≤ δ := by
+    refine (consistencyDefect_postprocess_question_le μ
+      (fun _ => A) (fun _ => B) ψ f).trans ?_
+    rw [consistencyDefect_const_eq μ hμ]
+    exact hcons
+  have hPBf : consistencyDefect μ
+      (fun x b => heteroKron ((P.postprocess (f x)).effect b) 1)
+      (fun x b => heteroKron 1 ((B.postprocess (f x)).effect b)) ψ ≤
+        δ + Real.sqrt (220 * Real.rpow δ (1 / 4 : ℝ)) := by
+    refine (consistencyDefect_postprocess_question_le μ
+      (fun _ => P) (fun _ => B) ψ f).trans ?_
+    rw [consistencyDefect_const_eq μ hμ]
+    exact hPB
+  simpa only [leftPlacedMeasurement, rightPlacedMeasurement,
+    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.ofSumEqOne] using consistencyDefect_trans_le μ
+    (fun x => leftPlacedMeasurement (P.postprocess (f x)))
+    (fun x => rightPlacedMeasurement (B.postprocess (f x)))
+    (fun x => leftPlacedMeasurement (A.postprocess (f x)))
+    (fun x => rightPlacedMeasurement (N x)) ψ _ δ η hμ hψ hPBf hABf hAN
+
+/-- Tensor-factor exchange intertwines the two Kronecker-product actions. -/
+private theorem applyOperatorToState_heteroKron_prodComm {ιA ιB : Type*}
+    [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
+    (A : Op ιA) (B : Op ιB) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)) :
+    applyOperatorToState (heteroKron B A) (reindexState (Equiv.prodComm ιA ιB) ψ) =
+      reindexState (Equiv.prodComm ιA ιB) (applyOperatorToState (heteroKron A B) ψ) := by
+  have hop : heteroKron B A =
+      (heteroKron A B).submatrix (Equiv.prodComm ιB ιA) (Equiv.prodComm ιB ιA) := by
+    ext i j
+    exact mul_comm _ _
+  apply (EuclideanSpace.equiv (ιB × ιA) ℂ).injective
+  change heteroKron B A *ᵥ (ψ.ofLp ∘ (Equiv.prodComm ιB ιA)) =
+    (heteroKron A B *ᵥ ψ.ofLp) ∘ (Equiv.prodComm ιB ιA)
+  rw [hop, Matrix.submatrix_mulVec_equiv _ _ _ (Equiv.prodComm ιB ιA)]
+  rfl
+
+private theorem stateQForm_heteroKron_prodComm {ιA ιB : Type*}
+    [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
+    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)) (A : Op ιA) (B : Op ιB) :
+    stateQForm (reindexState (Equiv.prodComm ιA ιB) ψ) (heteroKron B A) =
+      stateQForm ψ (heteroKron A B) := by
+  unfold stateQForm
+  rw [applyOperatorToState_heteroKron_prodComm]
+  exact congrArg Complex.re
+    ((LinearIsometryEquiv.piLpCongrLeft 2 ℂ ℂ (Equiv.prodComm ιA ιB)).inner_map_map
+      ψ (applyOperatorToState (heteroKron A B) ψ))
+
+/-- Formalization-only factor-exchange identity for `lem:ortho` and its
+transport through postprocessing. The state is explicitly reindexed; neither
+equal local spaces nor invariance of the state under exchange is assumed. -/
+theorem consistencyDefect_prodComm {X α ιA ιB : Type*}
+    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
+    [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
+    (μ : Distribution X) (A : X → α → Op ιA) (B : X → α → Op ιB)
+    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)) :
+    consistencyDefect μ (fun x a => heteroKron (B x a) 1)
+        (fun x a => heteroKron 1 (A x a)) (reindexState (Equiv.prodComm ιA ιB) ψ) =
+      consistencyDefect μ (fun x a => heteroKron (A x a) 1)
+        (fun x a => heteroKron 1 (B x a)) ψ := by
+  unfold consistencyDefect
+  simp_rw [consistency_term_eq_stateQForm, placed_product_stateQForm_eq,
+    stateQForm_heteroKron_prodComm]
+  apply avgOver_congr
+  intro x
+  rw [Finset.sum_comm]
+  simp only [eq_comm]
+
+/-- Formalization-only distance identity for the Bob-side rounding in
+`lem:ortho`: left placement on the exchanged state is right placement on the
+original state. The two local coordinate types may be different. -/
+theorem opFamilyDistSq_left_prodComm {X α ιA ιB : Type*}
+    [Fintype α] [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
+    (μ : Distribution X) (A B : X → α → Op ιB)
+    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)) :
+    opFamilyDistSq μ (fun x a => heteroKron (A x a) 1)
+        (fun x a => heteroKron (B x a) 1) (reindexState (Equiv.prodComm ιA ιB) ψ) =
+      opFamilyDistSq μ (fun x a => heteroKron 1 (A x a))
+        (fun x a => heteroKron 1 (B x a)) ψ := by
+  unfold opFamilyDistSq
+  simp_rw [← heteroKron_sub_left, applyOperatorToState_heteroKron_prodComm,
+    reindexState_norm_eq, heteroKron_sub_right]
+
+/-- Formalization-only Bob-side form of projective rounding and consistency
+transport for `lem:qld-4-7`. It follows by explicitly exchanging the tensor
+factors and applying the Alice-side theorem to the exchanged state. The error
+and normalization hypotheses are exactly those of the Alice-side form. -/
+theorem projective_rounding_preserves_postprocessed_consistency_right
+    {ιA ιB α : Type*}
+    [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
+    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
+    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)) (hψ : ‖ψ‖ = 1)
+    (A : Measurement α ιA) (B : Measurement α ιB) (δ : ℝ) (hδ : 0 ≤ δ)
+    (hcons : consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution Unit)
+      (fun _ a => heteroKron (A.effect a) 1)
+      (fun _ a => heteroKron 1 (B.effect a)) ψ ≤ δ) :
+    ∃ P : Measurement α ιB, Measurement.IsProjective P ∧
+      opFamilyDistSq (uniformDistribution Unit)
+        (fun _ a => heteroKron 1 (P.effect a))
+        (fun _ a => heteroKron 1 (B.effect a)) ψ ≤
+          220 * Real.rpow δ (1 / 4 : ℝ) ∧
+      ∀ {X β : Type*} [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β]
+        (μ : Distribution X), μ.IsProbability → ∀ (f : X → α → β)
+        (N : X → Measurement β ιA) (η : ℝ),
+        consistencyDefect μ
+          (fun x b => heteroKron ((N x).effect b) 1)
+          (fun x b => heteroKron 1 ((B.postprocess (f x)).effect b)) ψ ≤ η →
+        consistencyDefect μ
+          (fun x b => heteroKron ((N x).effect b) 1)
+          (fun x b => heteroKron 1 ((P.postprocess (f x)).effect b)) ψ ≤
+            δ + Real.sqrt (220 * Real.rpow δ (1 / 4 : ℝ)) +
+              2 * Real.sqrt (δ + η) := by
+  have hψ' : ‖reindexState (Equiv.prodComm ιA ιB) ψ‖ = 1 := by
+    rw [reindexState_norm_eq, hψ]
+  have hcons' : consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution Unit)
+      (fun _ a => heteroKron (B.effect a) 1)
+      (fun _ a => heteroKron 1 (A.effect a))
+      (reindexState (Equiv.prodComm ιA ιB) ψ) ≤ δ := by
+    rwa [consistencyDefect_prodComm]
+  obtain ⟨P, hP, hdist, htransport⟩ :=
+    projective_rounding_preserves_postprocessed_consistency_left
+      (reindexState (Equiv.prodComm ιA ιB) ψ) hψ' B A δ hδ hcons'
+  rw [opFamilyDistSq_left_prodComm] at hdist
+  refine ⟨P, hP, hdist, ?_⟩
+  intro X β _ _ _ _ μ hμ f N η hNB
+  have hNB' : consistencyDefect μ
+      (fun x b => heteroKron ((B.postprocess (f x)).effect b) 1)
+      (fun x b => heteroKron 1 ((N x).effect b))
+      (reindexState (Equiv.prodComm ιA ιB) ψ) ≤ η := by
+    rwa [consistencyDefect_prodComm]
+  have hout := htransport μ hμ f N η hNB'
+  rwa [consistencyDefect_prodComm] at hout
+
+/-- Formalization-only simultaneous rounding and transport for the compression
+step of `lem:qld-4-7`. A single pair of complete projective measurements on the
+original heterogeneous spaces satisfies the distance bounds and both consistency
+estimates for every finite question type, probability distribution, and
+question-dependent outcome map. Each comparison family requires only its own
+consistency bound against the corresponding unrounded POVM. The hypotheses are
+`‖ψ‖ = 1`, `δ ≥ 0`, and the original cross-player consistency bound; no range
+restriction on the comparison error or outcome-cardinality factor is imposed. -/
+theorem projective_rounding_preserves_postprocessed_consistency
+    {ιA ιB α : Type*}
+    [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
+    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
+    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)) (hψ : ‖ψ‖ = 1)
+    (A : Measurement α ιA) (B : Measurement α ιB) (δ : ℝ) (hδ : 0 ≤ δ)
+    (hcons : consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution Unit)
+      (fun _ a => heteroKron (A.effect a) 1)
+      (fun _ a => heteroKron 1 (B.effect a)) ψ ≤ δ) :
+    ∃ PA : Measurement α ιA, ∃ PB : Measurement α ιB,
+      Measurement.IsProjective PA ∧ Measurement.IsProjective PB ∧
+      opFamilyDistSq (uniformDistribution Unit)
+        (fun _ a => heteroKron (PA.effect a) 1)
+        (fun _ a => heteroKron (A.effect a) 1) ψ ≤
+          220 * Real.rpow δ (1 / 4 : ℝ) ∧
+      opFamilyDistSq (uniformDistribution Unit)
+        (fun _ a => heteroKron 1 (PB.effect a))
+        (fun _ a => heteroKron 1 (B.effect a)) ψ ≤
+          220 * Real.rpow δ (1 / 4 : ℝ) ∧
+      ∀ {X β : Type*} [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β]
+        (μ : Distribution X), μ.IsProbability → ∀ (f : X → α → β),
+        (∀ (N : X → Measurement β ιB) (η : ℝ),
+          consistencyDefect μ
+            (fun x b => heteroKron ((A.postprocess (f x)).effect b) 1)
+            (fun x b => heteroKron 1 ((N x).effect b)) ψ ≤ η →
+          consistencyDefect μ
+            (fun x b => heteroKron ((PA.postprocess (f x)).effect b) 1)
+            (fun x b => heteroKron 1 ((N x).effect b)) ψ ≤
+              δ + Real.sqrt (220 * Real.rpow δ (1 / 4 : ℝ)) +
+                2 * Real.sqrt (δ + η)) ∧
+        (∀ (N : X → Measurement β ιA) (η : ℝ),
+          consistencyDefect μ
+            (fun x b => heteroKron ((N x).effect b) 1)
+            (fun x b => heteroKron 1 ((B.postprocess (f x)).effect b)) ψ ≤ η →
+          consistencyDefect μ
+            (fun x b => heteroKron ((N x).effect b) 1)
+            (fun x b => heteroKron 1 ((PB.postprocess (f x)).effect b)) ψ ≤
+              δ + Real.sqrt (220 * Real.rpow δ (1 / 4 : ℝ)) +
+                2 * Real.sqrt (δ + η)) := by
+  obtain ⟨PA, hPA, hAdist, hAtransport⟩ :=
+    projective_rounding_preserves_postprocessed_consistency_left ψ hψ A B δ hδ hcons
+  obtain ⟨PB, hPB, hBdist, hBtransport⟩ :=
+    projective_rounding_preserves_postprocessed_consistency_right ψ hψ A B δ hδ hcons
+  refine ⟨PA, PB, hPA, hPB, hAdist, hBdist, ?_⟩
+  intro X β _ _ _ _ μ hμ f
+  exact ⟨hAtransport μ hμ f, hBtransport μ hμ f⟩
+
+end
+
+end MIPStarRE.QPBT

@@ -0,0 +1,170 @@
+import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Games.StrategyClasses
+
+/-! # Ground-coordinate compression of finite measurements
+
+For a distinguished ancilla coordinate `k₀`, `groundCompressMeasurement k₀ M`
+has effects `M.effect a (i, k₀) (j, k₀)`. Positivity and completeness descend
+to this principal submatrix. Compression commutes with finite outcome
+postprocessing and preserves bipartite consistency exactly on `padState`.
+The two players' spaces and their ancilla spaces may all be different.
+
+These are Lean-only auxiliaries for the two Naimark steps in the proof of
+`lem:qld-4-7`, tracked by issue #277. They allow measurements on the enlarged
+spaces to be compared on the original spaces, including after polynomial
+evaluation. Compression does not in general preserve projectivity; obtaining
+projective measurements on the original spaces requires a separate rounding
+argument. No statement of `lem:qld-4-7` is formalized here.
+
+## References
+
+* `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1278-1288`,
+  the two Naimark steps in the proof of `lem:qld-4-7`.
+* `references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:232-248`,
+  `def:consistency`.
+-/
+
+namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
+
+open scoped BigOperators MatrixOrder ComplexOrder
+open MIPStarRE.LDT MIPStarRE.Quantum
+
+noncomputable section
+
+section Measurement
+
+variable {α β I K : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype β]
+  [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I] [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K]
+
+/-- Compress every effect of a finite POVM to the coordinate `k₀` of its
+ancilla. This is the POVM with effects `J† M_a J`, where `J` inserts `k₀`.
+Positivity follows from `Matrix.PosSemidef.submatrix`, and completeness from
+the injectivity of the coordinate inclusion. -/
+def groundCompressMeasurement (k₀ : K) (M : Quantum.Measurement α (I × K)) :
+    Quantum.Measurement α I :=
+  Quantum.Measurement.ofSumEqOne
+    (fun a => (M.effect a).submatrix (fun i => (i, k₀)) (fun i => (i, k₀)))
+    (fun a => Matrix.nonneg_iff_posSemidef.mpr
+      ((Matrix.nonneg_iff_posSemidef.mp (M.pos a)).submatrix _)) <| by
+    ext i j
+    simpa [Matrix.sum_apply, Matrix.submatrix_apply, Matrix.one_apply] using
+      congrArg (fun T : Op (I × K) => T (i, k₀) (j, k₀)) M.sum_eq_one
+
+/-- The compressed effect is the principal submatrix at `k₀`. -/
+@[simp] theorem ground_compress_measurement_effect
+    (k₀ : K) (M : Quantum.Measurement α (I × K)) (a : α) (i j : I) :
+    (groundCompressMeasurement k₀ M).effect a i j =
+      M.effect a (i, k₀) (j, k₀) := rfl
+
+/-- Ground-coordinate compression commutes with arbitrary finite relabeling
+of outcomes, since taking a submatrix commutes with each fiber sum. -/
+@[simp] theorem ground_compress_measurement_postprocess
+    [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
+    (k₀ : K) (M : Quantum.Measurement α (I × K)) (f : α → β) :
+    groundCompressMeasurement k₀ (M.postprocess f) =
+      (groundCompressMeasurement k₀ M).postprocess f := by
+  apply Quantum.Measurement.ext
+  intro b
+  ext i j
+  simp only [ground_compress_measurement_effect, Quantum.Measurement.postprocess_effect,
+    Matrix.sum_apply]
+
+end Measurement
+
+section Bipartite
+
+variable {X α β I J K L : Type*}
+  [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype α] [Fintype β]
+  [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I] [Fintype J] [DecidableEq J]
+  [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K] [Fintype L] [DecidableEq L]
+
+/-- Every bipartite outcome correlation on the independently padded state
+equals the correlation of the compressed POVMs on the original state.
+Neither normalization nor equality of the player spaces is required. -/
+theorem vector_qform_ground_compress_measurement
+    (k₀ : K) (l₀ : L) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (I × J))
+    (A : Quantum.Measurement α (I × K)) (B : Quantum.Measurement β (J × L))
+    (a : α) (b : β) :
+    vectorQForm (padState k₀ l₀ ψ) (heteroKron (A.effect a) (B.effect b)) =
+      vectorQForm ψ (heteroKron
+        ((groundCompressMeasurement k₀ A).effect a)
+        ((groundCompressMeasurement l₀ B).effect b)) := by
+  exact stateQForm_padState k₀ l₀ ψ _ _ _ _ (fun _ _ => rfl) (fun _ _ => rfl)
+
+/-- The averaged off-diagonal consistency defect is exactly preserved by
+ground-coordinate compression on independently padded bipartite states.
+This applies to any finite question distribution and any pair of POVM families. -/
+theorem consistency_defect_ground_compress_measurement [DecidableEq α]
+    (μ : Distribution X) (k₀ : K) (l₀ : L) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (I × J))
+    (A : X → Quantum.Measurement α (I × K))
+    (B : X → Quantum.Measurement α (J × L)) :
+    consistencyDefect μ
+        (fun x a => heteroKron ((A x).effect a) 1)
+        (fun x a => heteroKron 1 ((B x).effect a)) (padState k₀ l₀ ψ) =
+      consistencyDefect μ
+        (fun x a => heteroKron ((groundCompressMeasurement k₀ (A x)).effect a) 1)
+        (fun x a => heteroKron 1 ((groundCompressMeasurement l₀ (B x)).effect a)) ψ := by
+  unfold consistencyDefect
+  apply avgOver_congr
+  intro x
+  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
+  intro a _
+  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
+  intro b _
+  split_ifs with hab
+  · rfl
+  · simp only [heteroKron_mul, mul_one, one_mul]
+    exact vector_qform_ground_compress_measurement k₀ l₀ ψ (A x) (B x) a b
+
+/-- A consistency bound holds on the independently padded state if and only
+if the same bound holds for the compressed measurements on the original state. -/
+theorem is_consistent_within_ground_compress_measurement_iff [DecidableEq α]
+    (μ : Distribution X) (k₀ : K) (l₀ : L) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (I × J))
+    (A : X → Quantum.Measurement α (I × K))
+    (B : X → Quantum.Measurement α (J × L)) (δ : ℝ) :
+    IsConsistentWithin μ
+        (fun x a => heteroKron ((A x).effect a) 1)
+        (fun x a => heteroKron 1 ((B x).effect a)) (padState k₀ l₀ ψ) δ ↔
+      IsConsistentWithin μ
+        (fun x a => heteroKron ((groundCompressMeasurement k₀ (A x)).effect a) 1)
+        (fun x a => heteroKron 1 ((groundCompressMeasurement l₀ (B x)).effect a)) ψ δ := by
+  unfold IsConsistentWithin
+  rw [consistency_defect_ground_compress_measurement]
+
+/-- Exact consistency preservation also holds after question-dependent
+postprocessing. The original outcome types and the two outcome maps may
+differ; only the final outcome alphabet is shared. In the application to
+`lem:qld-4-7`, these maps include evaluation of the polynomial outcomes. -/
+theorem consistency_defect_ground_compress_measurement_postprocess
+    {γ : Type*} [Fintype γ] [DecidableEq γ] [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
+    (μ : Distribution X) (k₀ : K) (l₀ : L) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (I × J))
+    (A : X → Quantum.Measurement α (I × K))
+    (B : X → Quantum.Measurement β (J × L)) (f : X → α → γ) (g : X → β → γ) :
+    consistencyDefect μ
+        (fun x c => heteroKron (((A x).postprocess (f x)).effect c) 1)
+        (fun x c => heteroKron 1 (((B x).postprocess (g x)).effect c))
+        (padState k₀ l₀ ψ) =
+      consistencyDefect μ
+        (fun x c => heteroKron
+          (((groundCompressMeasurement k₀ (A x)).postprocess (f x)).effect c) 1)
+        (fun x c => heteroKron 1
+          (((groundCompressMeasurement l₀ (B x)).postprocess (g x)).effect c)) ψ := by
+  simpa only [ground_compress_measurement_postprocess] using
+    consistency_defect_ground_compress_measurement μ k₀ l₀ ψ
+      (fun x => (A x).postprocess (f x)) (fun x => (B x).postprocess (g x))
+
+end Bipartite
+
+/-- Compressing the existing completed Naimark dilation at `none` recovers
+the original POVM as a measurement, by its established effect identity. -/
+@[simp] theorem ground_compress_dilated_measurement
+    {α I : Type} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I]
+    (a₀ : α) (M : Quantum.Measurement α I) :
+    groundCompressMeasurement none (dilatedMeasurement a₀ M) = M := by
+  apply Quantum.Measurement.ext
+  intro a
+  ext i j
+  exact dilatedMeasurement_compression a₀ a M i j
+
+end
+
+end MIPStarRE.QPBT
